claims.text: PtPdRhRuIrOs solid-solution catalysts can catalyze ethanol oxidation through a complete 12-electron process.
High configurational disorder in PtPdRhRuIrOs induces lattice distortions.
Disorder-induced lattice distortions create isolated, electronically perturbed metal sites.
Electronically perturbed sites modify the adsorption strengths of ethanol-oxidation intermediates.
The modified adsorption strengths favor complete 12-electron ethanol oxidation.
The disorder-created sites enhance catalyst durability.
The as-synthesized PtPdRhRuIrOs catalyst has high lattice strain and a random atomic-site distribution.
Mild thermal annealing can partially reduce local lattice disorder and promote local ordering in the catalyst.
Local electronic structures of neighboring active sites in compositionally heterogeneous alloys can influence reaction selectivity.
Reducing disorder by annealing will diminish the distinctive local electronic effects of the disordered catalyst.
The highly disordered baseline catalyst will have a higher proportion of complete 12-electron oxidation products than the partially ordered catalyst.
Partial ordering by annealing will shift ethanol oxidation toward a more limited pathway, potentially near a 4-electron process.
The partially ordered catalyst will deactivate faster than the highly disordered baseline.
The proposed disorder-dependent mechanism is expected to hold for particles smaller than 10 nm.
The proposed mechanism is expected to hold at reaction temperatures up to approximately 80 degrees Celsius.
At higher temperatures, significant sintering or phase segregation may dominate catalyst behavior.
